next_step: Run 72hr perf POC with 3 model variants; deliver latency and cost breakdown by 2025-02-20
notes:
Account background:
- Stillwater builds low-latency conversational agents for trading desk assistants and live customer support (market data + policy lookup). High QPS peaks during market open/close windows.
- CTO (Aaron Delgado): 'We need deterministic SLOs during spikes, otherwise traders complain.'

Recent timeline / activity (shorthand):
- 2025-01-22: Intro call (Maya) — product fit looks promising; asked for architecture overview. (ff_2025-01-22_StillwaterKickoff)
- 2025-02-05: Deep-dive w/ infra + security (Ethan + Priya) — security wants SOC2 + KMS flow; also asked for network diagram. (ff_2025-02-05_latency-review)
- 2025-02-08: Sent pricing deck + baseline perf ask (drive link).
- 2025-02-12: Confirmed POC scope and metrics (timeline below).

Use-case & technical requirements (from product/infra teams):
- Workloads: synchronous chat + short-form summarization + reranking for search results. Most requests target <= 256 tokens.
- Latency targets: p50 < 30ms for the fastest path, p95 < 80ms, p99 < 150ms (tight window during spikes).
- Throughput: baseline 120 qps, burst to 800 qps during market events.
- Cost sensitivity: target reduce per-token inference cost by 2-3x vs current self-hosted float32 baseline.
- Model preferences: open 13B-class models (quantized variants), fallback to smaller 7B for extreme load. Interested in Redwood "quantized" + batching guidance.
- Routing & fallback: need region-aware routing (US primary, EU backup) and auto-fallback to cheaper model variant on capacity pressure.
- Persistence & caching: strong interest in prefix caching for repeated dialogs and KV re-use across session.

Optimize interest (specific asks):
- Batching: guidance on micro-batch sizes for sub-50ms median with controlled tail latencies; expected batching window <= 10ms for live chat.
- Caching: prefix vs KV cache tradeoffs for multi-turn agent sessions; want examples of cache hit rate impact on cost/latency.
- Quantization: validate 4-bit/LLM.int8-like profiles for their 13B models; ask for quality vs token-cost matrix.
- Perf benchmarking: request canonical test harness from Redwood (replay logs + synthetic spikes), want side-by-side of hosted vs Dedicated with same workload.

POC plan (agreed):
- 72hr perf run (start 2025-02-16) with three model variants: quant-13B, int8-13B, small-7B.
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, qps sustained, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, cache hit rate impact.
- Deliverable: single report + recommendations (batch sizes, cache TTLs, quant profile) and a sample autoscaling policy.

Quotes / callouts from meetings:
- "If we can hit p95 <80ms and 2x cost savings vs our baseline, we can justify replacing current infra." — Head of ML Ops
- Security: 'Need proof of KMS integration and retention controls before infra access' — Security lead

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal: NDA routing; blocks access to SOC2 artifact until signed.
- Data residency: some test datasets include EU customer PII — need routing to EU region for those sessions.
- Budget: procurement team needs ARR band confirmation to proceed with Dedicated pricing.

Suggested next actions (for AE/SE):
- Deliver Redwood POC package + perf harness link and onboarding checklist by 2025-02-14.
- SE to propose batching profile (initial: micro-batch 8, adaptive up to 32) and cache TTL recommendations.
- Get security checklist and KMS example integration docs to customer legal/security.

CRM shorthand / internal notes:
- High conviction (product + finance aligned) if POC meets latency & cost targets.
- Competitive risk: they will evaluate OpenAI + Vertex for hosted fallback; emphasize Dedicated predictable throughput.
- Close target: 2025-03 if POC successful.
